title: Run a program with cost
statement: Fix a dimension, an access mode, an output type, and a Boolean target function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Running a learning program with cost produces a probability distribution on pairs of outputs and learning costs: a pure return has zero cost; a random bit costs one unit of local work; each random labeled example costs one example call and one unit of work; a batch of $m$ labeled examples costs $m$ example calls and $m$ units of work; a batch of $m$ uniform cube inputs costs $mn$ units of work; and a matrix indexed by a finite set $I$ with $m$ examples per index costs $|I|m$ example calls and $|I|m$ units of work. A matrix-output operation uses that same matrix cost plus its specified work charge, a membership query costs one query and one unit of work, and an explicitly charged computation costs its specified number of work units.

matrix operations use a finite index set
batch sizes and work charges are natural numbers
